sources.note: Bibliography only; names Benor 2009 JQR, Benor 2012 Becoming Frum, Benor 2018 (De Gruyter chapter), Burdin 2017 JJL (rise-fall intonation contour), Fader 2009, Fishman 1985 as the core Jewish English literature.
Bookkeeping entry: 'Merged into English [eng]; entirely intelligible with English'; change request 2006-044, effective 2007-07-18; no references listed.
Nothing on stress or prosody; 'Yeshivish' cites Baumel 2006 that Yeshivish 'differs from English primarily in phonemic structure, lexical meaning, and syntax'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / John Cowan. 2006. Change Request 2006-044: retire [yib] Yinglish, merge into [eng] (adopted 2007-07-18). SIL International, 7 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.2: Yinglish is 'a dialect with Yiddish-derived vocabulary and occasional aberrant Yiddish-derived syntax' that 'fits smoothly into the English dialect continuum'; '(Some borrowed words have un-English phonologies, but so do "Bach" and "oeuvre" as pronounced by many English speakers.)'

Contributor instruction only: transcriptions 'should use capital letters for the stressed syllable, such as "shah-BAHT" or "SHAH-biss"' (i.e., final vs penultimate stress on Hebrew loanwords depends on Israeli vs Ashkenazi source form); no rule stated.
